business_ops.seasonality: Under 'Seasonality and Project Timing' in Principal Factors affecting our Results of Operations, the DRHP states: 'Execution timelines may be affected by factors such as festive seasons, monsoons, or client-specific business cycles, leading to uneven revenue recognition across periods.' business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration into component manufacture: in addition to site-based contracting services, the Company operates an in-house manufacturing facility (Mettukuppam, Chennai, 5000 Sq Ft) engaged in the fabrication of customised furniture, joinery and fit-out components, and concurrently undertakes Cushion and Upholstery Work for seating and soft-furnishing components. The DRHP states this in-house manufacturing capability enables the Company to exercise direct quality control over finished components, optimise production timelines and deliver customised fit-out elements aligned with the specific design and functional requirements of each project. Inputs are sourced through a structured procurement process from a network of pre-approved manufacturers, suppliers and vendors, with multiple quotations obtained and evaluated on technical specifications, pricing, delivery timelines and vendor reliability, and quality checks and inspections on delivery; plywood is procured from approved suppliers against specified thickness, grade (e.g. MR or BWR) and dimensions, and is then processed in-house through laminate/veneer pasting, cutting and sizing, edge banding, upholstery and assembly before handover to the client. Downstream, the Company both contracts directly with clients and executes work on a sub-contracting basis (Rs. 1,640.50 lakhs, 38.25% of revenue from operations for the period ended February 28, 2026), and engages multiple vendors and contractors for specialized work. State-wise raw material procurement for the period ended February 28, 2026 totalled Rs. 3,096.92 lakhs, of which Tamil Nadu was 72.77%, Telangana 15.05%, Karnataka 3.25%, Kerala 3.15%, Odisha 2.39% and Maharashtra 2.12%.

overview.business_model: The Company executes interior contracting projects against work orders and agreements issued by clients, covering interior works (partitions, false ceilings, wall panelling, carpentry and joinery, doors, finishes, storage units, workstations, cabins, conference rooms), mechanical/HVAC works (ducting, insulation, copper piping, cassette units, chillers, AHUs, dampers, diffusers, grilles), electrical works (panels and distribution boards, cables and cable trays, conduiting and wiring, lighting fixtures, UPS and battery systems, switches, sockets and isolators, fire alarm and sprinkler systems, earthing works) and final finishing and fit-out activities, taking spaces from bare shell structures to fully furnished and operational commercial spaces. Alongside site-based contracting, the Company operates an in-house manufacturing facility fabricating customised furniture, joinery and fit-out components and undertaking cushion and upholstery work for seating and soft-furnishing components, which the DRHP states enables direct quality control over finished components and optimised production timelines. End markets stated are corporate offices, research and development facilities, laboratories, lounges, flexible workspaces, hospitals, commercial retail outlets and other specialized environments.

It states the interior fit-out industry in which it operates is highly fragmented and competitive with the presence of numerous organized and unorganized players offering similar products and services, and that increased competition may lead to pricing pressures, reduced profit margins, loss of market share, and challenges in securing new projects or retaining existing clients, which could adversely affect business operations, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.
strategy_growth.evidence: Risk factor 25. No market share or named competitors are stated in this risk factor.

strategy_growth.detail: The DRHP states that if the Company is unable to source business opportunities effectively it may not achieve its financial objectives, and that its ability to do so depends on its ability to identify, evaluate and accomplish business opportunities. It states that to grow the business it will need to hire, train, supervise and manage new employees, expand its distribution network and implement systems capable of effectively accommodating its growth, with no assurance such employees will contribute to the success of the business or that such systems will be implemented effectively. It states failure to source business opportunities effectively could have a material adverse effect on business, financial condition and results of operations, that the strategies used in the future may differ from those presently in use, and that no assurance can be given that its analyses of market and other data, or the strategies it uses or plans to use, will be successful under various market conditions.

concerns_observed: Cash generation runs against reported profit: CFO was minus Rs 128.96 lakhs (FY2023), minus Rs 463.03 lakhs (FY2024), plus Rs 589.86 lakhs (FY2025) and minus Rs 1,158.37 lakhs in the stub - negative in three of four periods, and most negative in the period carrying the highest PAT (Rs 753.31 lakhs). Closing cash at February 28, 2026 is Rs 54.23 lakhs, inside which Rs 32.05 lakhs is restricted (nil restricted in all three prior periods).

The working-capital cycle deteriorated on both legs: debtor days 28 (FY2023) to 64 to 57 to 142 (stub) and inventory days 155 to 189 to 253 to 285, taking trade receivables to Rs 1,825.48 lakhs and inventories to Rs 2,350.93 lakhs; net working capital as stated in the DRHP moved Rs 175.33 / 603.24 / 438.78 / 1,823.54 lakhs against net worth of Rs 2,065.57 lakhs.

The only manufacturing facility (5,000 sq ft) and the warehouse, both at Krishna Industrial Estate, Vanagaram, Chennai, are held on leave and licence from a single landlord, Mr K.C. Saravanan, with an expiry date of January 03, 2027 - roughly seven months after the DRHP date of June 11, 2026 - while commercial operations at the replacement Kundrathur facility are stated as 6-9 months from receipt of Net Proceeds.

Pre-issue leverage is short-dated and personally secured: total borrowings Rs 1,614.12 lakhs at February 28, 2026 (long-term Rs 285.92, short-term Rs 1,328.20) against net worth of Rs 2,065.57 lakhs; HDFC working capital drawn Rs 815.61 lakhs of a Rs 900.00 lakhs sanction; unsecured loans from banks and financial institutions Rs 650.51 lakhs; a factoring line from Arth Padarth Factors And Finance Private Limited at 17.00% p.a.; security includes personal guarantees of all directors and the promoters' residential flats at Alwarthirunagar and Velan Nagar, Valasaravakkam, Chennai.

Margin is a thin residual over a commodity input bought without commitments: cost of materials consumed was 91.89% of total expenses (FY2023), 86.33% (FY2024), 84.07% (FY2025) and 83.91% (Rs 2,756.59 lakhs, stub), and the DRHP states there are no continuing or exclusive arrangements with suppliers - purchases run on work orders with no firm quantities at fixed prices, so price increases cannot be resisted contractually.

Comparability is limited in two directions at once: the latest period is an 11-month stub (April 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026) set beside 12-month fiscal years, and the stub and FY2025 come from special-purpose statements audited by M N H & Co (reports dated May 8, 2026) while FY2024 and FY2023 come from statutory statements audited by the previous auditor M S Pandian & Co (reports dated September 7, 2024 and September 7, 2023).

The whole senior and independent layer was constituted two months before filing: CFO Lanka Vishwanath Bharath and Company Secretary Pinki Sharma both since April 10, 2026; Independent Directors Vinod Kumar Narva and Jaya Sri Musthyala both appointed April 10, 2026 and both also directors of the same other company, EPW India Limited; the board is 5 with 2 independent and 3 committees; the third non-executive director, Packirysamy Sundaramoorthy (62, Promoter Group), is stated to hold no qualification degree and no experience is set out for him.

Revenue swings violently between principal and sub-contract work: the contractor / sub-contractor split ran 60.89% / 39.11% (FY2023), 87.41% / 12.59% (FY2024), 47.48% / 52.52% (FY2025) and 61.75% / 38.25% (stub) - and sub-contract work is governed by terms set by the primary contractor, with early termination or financial penalties as the stated failure mode.

Contingent liabilities of Rs 143.60 lakhs appear for the first time at February 28, 2026 - bank guarantees and letters of credit Rs 81.87 lakhs and GST matters Rs 61.73 lakhs, 22.87% of net worth - against dashes in all three prior years for every line.

No long-term or exclusive client agreements exist at all; the DRHP states work is governed by work orders placed from time to time, that the number of work orders differs from period to period, and that this has already caused revenues, results and cash flows to fluctuate - with the Order Book itself carrying the caution that it may not be representative of future results.

Client insurance cover is narrow for a site-execution business: policies cover stock at the manufacturing facility and warehouse, stock at specific project sites, and workmen compensation for selected project sites only; loss of profits and terrorism are expressly not covered.

The DRHP states no employee headcount anywhere in the routed sections for a business whose execution depends on carpenters, painters, electricians and other site workers engaged as third-party service providers (risk factor 18), and records key awards, certifications and recognitions as NIL apart from ISO 9001:2015.
data_gaps: The Offer is at DRHP stage, so Issue Price, floor and cap, aggregate issue size, Net Proceeds, the General Corporate Purposes amount, post-Issue capital, the Promoters' post-Issue percentage, issue programme dates, market maker, underwriter, syndicate member and bankers to the Issue all print as placeholders. No valuation, market capitalisation or P/E can be stated from this document. This is a filing-stage fact rather than a company weakness.

The Net Proceeds deployment table (certificate of M N H & Co, UDIN 26254857DXXGVP8852) prints a placeholder against every year for every object, so no object can be tied to a fiscal year - the only year-attributed figure anywhere is the Rs 1,500.00 lakhs of working capital placed against March 31, 2027 in the separate funding-pattern table.

14 of the 22 related-party rows carry no amount. The AS 18 note's row labels and numeric cells were emitted out of order by the PDF text layer and the note prints no sub-total to reconcile against, so promoter remuneration, rent, loans taken, loans repaid, loans converted to equity, issue of equity share capital, the February 28, 2026 Life Style Modular purchase column, and the Part C closing balances (director remuneration payable, dues to directors, loan payable) are left null and were not inferred. The risk-factor chapter was mis-filed by the document's own chapter routing and recovered late; 48 numbered risk factors were retrieved (internal operational 17, financial 16, compliance 11, strategy 4). Separately, the Delayed ROC Filings table prints serials 1-20 then 23-24, so rows 21 and 22 of that table are absent from the extract.

Trade receivables ageing is absent from the routed text - only trade payables ageing is present - so the Rs 1,825.48 lakhs receivable balance at February 28, 2026 cannot be aged and no over-one-year bucket can be stated. Debtor days of 142 are the only ageing proxy available.

The DRHP states there are no listed companies whose business operations are similar to the Company's or of a comparable size and that it is therefore not possible to provide an industry comparison. The empty peer set is the issuer's own disclosure, and it means no external P/E, RoNW, margin or working-capital benchmark exists for this business from the document.

Facility-level debt is not recoverable for three of four disclosed lines: the Axis Bank row carries the tokens '-', '-2.22', '160.86' and '182.34' with unresolvable column alignment (and a March 31, 2023 balance would predate the December 14, 2023 sanction), while Arth Padarth Factors (Rs 100.00 lakhs sanctioned, 17.00% p.a.) and the interest-free loans from directors and relatives carry no printed outstanding. The long-term borrowings annexure is not in the routed text, so the loan list does not sum to the Rs 1,614.12 lakhs total.

Employee headcount is not stated anywhere in the routed sections - only that the team consists of designers and project management professionals - so no labour cost, attrition, direct-versus-contract split or revenue-per-employee figure can be established.
The Offer for Sale of up to 10,00,000 shares has no selling shareholder named and no percentage of Offer stated in the routed text.

The entire Promoter's Contribution three-year lock-in table is a placeholder for both Mugundhan Sekar and Ishwarya Packirysamy (dates, nature of issue, share count, face value, issue price, pre and post-Issue percentages); only the '3 Years' period is stated. No promoter-excess lock-in, other pre-Issue lock-in or anchor lock-in period or expiry date appears, and Table I of the shareholding pattern shows nil shares currently locked in.

The contractor versus sub-contractor labels conflict inside the source itself: the business chapter's revenue split records 61.75% (stub) as 'Revenue earned as Contractor' and Rs 1,640.50 lakhs / 38.25% as sub-contracting, while risk factor 7 labels Rs 2,648.81 lakhs / 61.75% as sub-contractor and Rs 1,640.50 lakhs / 38.25% as contractor. The 61.75 / 38.25 split is certain in every period; which side of it is principal work is not.

Creditor days and the cash conversion cycle are not printed for any of the four periods - only debtor days and inventory days - so the working-capital cycle cannot be stated as a single number despite trade payables of Rs 1,575.53 lakhs at February 28, 2026.

No revenue split is printed across the stated end-use environments (corporate offices, R&D facilities, laboratories, lounges, flexible workspaces, hospitals, commercial retail), no client is named anywhere in the routed text, and the Order Book is disclosed only in aggregate across 12 projects.

No 'Our Group Companies' chapter is present in the routed text, so Life Style Modular Private Limited's revenue, profit, net worth and the terms and duration of the stated non-compete agreement cannot be assessed. Pages 80 and 85 of the Objects chapter are image-locked, so some rows in that chapter may be absent from the extract rather than absent from the DRHP.

An EPS conflict inside the document was resolved deliberately rather than left open: the series Rs 6.36 / 3.00 / 0.99 / 0.62 is taken post-bonus as printed on the primary restated statement of profit and loss, in preference to the ratio table's pre-bonus Rs 140.01 / 66.04 / 21.77 / 13.61. Return ratios other than RoNW (36.47% for the 11-month stub and not annualised, 52.59%, 36.56%, 36.02%, weighted average 44.49%) are not printed - no RoE or RoCE percentage appears in the routed text.

The new facility is 9,266 sq ft against the existing 5,000 sq ft. What incremental capacity does it add per product line, does the Vanagaram unit continue alongside it or is it replaced, and on what demand evidence beyond the current utilisation rates is the Rs 760.00 lakhs sized?

How many people does the Company employ directly, and how much of the Rs 2,756.59 lakhs cost of materials consumed is accompanied by payments to the third-party carpenters, painters, electricians and site workers named in risk factor 18 - no headcount, labour cost or attrition figure appears anywhere in the routed text?

verdict.our_read: Chennai end-to-end interior fit-out contractor (11-month stub to February 28, 2026: revenue Rs 4,289.31 lakhs, EBITDA margin 28.20% against 6.28% in FY2023, PAT Rs 753.31 lakhs) whose entire step-up sits on a period in which CFO was minus Rs 1,158.37 lakhs as trade receivables rose Rs 1,313.99 lakhs and inventories Rs 689.48 lakhs - and Rs 1,500.00 lakhs of the Net Proceeds, the largest single object, is asked for to fund more of the same working capital.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue Rs 1,861.62 / 2,827.25 / 3,297.48 / 4,289.31 lakhs, EBITDA margin 6.28% / 9.53% / 18.96% / 28.20%, PAT Rs 68.03 / 108.84 / 330.18 / 753.31 lakhs and EPS Rs 0.62 / 0.99 / 3.00 / 6.36 (post-bonus, as printed on the restated P&L) - a genuine and monotonic improvement. Marked down because the sharpest leg is an 11-month stub set against 12-month years, the stub and FY2025 were audited by M N H & Co while FY2024 and FY2023 came from the prior auditor M S Pandian & Co, and no explanation of the margin expansion is printed while cost of materials barely moved (86.33% to 84.07% to 83.91% of total expenses).

parameter_scores.basis: CFO minus Rs 128.96 / minus 463.03 / plus 589.86 / minus 1,158.37 lakhs - negative in three of four periods and worst in the highest-PAT period; closing cash Rs 54.23 lakhs of which Rs 32.05 lakhs restricted; borrowings Rs 1,614.12 lakhs (short-term Rs 1,328.20) against net worth Rs 2,065.57 lakhs; HDFC drawn Rs 815.61 lakhs of Rs 900.00 lakhs; a 17.00% factoring line; debtor days 142 and inventory days 285. Credit for net worth compounding from Rs 188.85 to Rs 2,065.57 lakhs and for all three cross-checks tying in all four periods.

Order Book of Rs 1,968.19 lakhs unexecuted out of Rs 4,226.72 lakhs across 12 ongoing projects at February 28, 2026, plus more than 50 projects completed over three years and the stub, is real forward evidence. Against it: no long-term or exclusive client agreements exist, work is governed by work orders whose number differs period to period, the DRHP itself cautions the Order Book may not be representative of future results, and no client is named anywhere in the routed text.

Objects are specific and costed - new facility Rs 760.00 lakhs (land lease 150.00, construction 250.00, plant and machinery 360.00), incremental working capital Rs 1,500.00 lakhs, repayment of unsecured borrowings Rs 240.00 lakhs, GCP capped at 15% of Gross Proceeds or Rs 1,000.00 lakhs whichever lower. Held down because no orders are placed and no definitive procurement agreements exist (the chapter never claims otherwise), the land is an MoU dated June 2, 2026 only, deployment has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution, no monitoring agency will be appointed (Issue below Rs 5,000.00 lakhs), the year-wise deployment table prints placeholders throughout, and the construction line is allocated Rs 250.00 lakhs against an engineer-certified Rs 252.88 lakhs and a third-party quotation of Rs 295.26 lakhs.

parameter_scores.basis: The demand case is better than most: all five product lines at the 5,000 sq ft Vanagaram unit run at 83.19% to 95.22% utilisation and installed capacity has been raised every year. The execution case is weak: the 9,266 sq ft Kundrathur land is unacquired with the 99-year lease deed to be registered only after Net Proceeds, machinery quotations dated May 21-29, 2026 carry 60-day / 8-week / 180-day validities the DRHP warns may lapse (escalation to be met from internal accruals), commercial operations are 6-9 months from receipt of Net Proceeds, and the existing plant's leave and licence expires January 03, 2027.

24 delayed ROC filings including an MGT-14 approximately 1,233 days late (due 29-11-2022, filed 15-05-2026); 17 EPF and 16 ESIC delayed remittances running into December 2025 dues; GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B delays up to 33 and 41 days continuing into the March 2026 return; quarterly current-asset statements to lenders only 'generally in agreement' with the books, unquantified. Board of 5 with only 2 independent directors, both appointed April 10, 2026 and both on the same other board (EPW India Limited); CFO and Company Secretary appointed the same day; three committees constituted. Credit for nil pledge, no SEBI or exchange action in five Fiscals, and an examination report with no qualification requiring adjustment.

The AS 18 disclosure is genuine and names Life Style Modular Private Limited as an enterprise over which the KMPs exercise significant influence, with purchases of Rs 30.00 / 24.48 / 48.94 lakhs cross-footing to a Rs 73.42 lakhs trade payable at March 31, 2025 - and risk factor 33 concedes the entity is in Interior Designing, the same line of business, with both promoters as its directors. A non-compete agreement is asserted with no terms, duration or financials disclosed, and no Group Companies chapter is present in the routed text. Absolute amounts are small relative to Rs 2,756.59 lakhs of material cost, which limits the downgrade.

Promoters hold 86.67% pre-Issue across 2 holders with nil pledge, have given personal guarantees and pledged personal residential properties as collateral, and converted Rs 49.00 lakhs of loans into equity on March 27, 2023. Against that: a face-value split on May 7, 2026 followed by a 1:10 bonus on May 08, 2026 (inside 18 months of the DRHP), a certified average cost of acquisition of Rs 0.45 per share against outside placements at Rs 780 and Rs 1,000 per pre-split share in 2025, an Offer for Sale of up to 10,00,000 shares with no selling shareholder identified in the routed text, a register of 19 shareholders, and post-Issue holding plus the entire three-year lock-in table left as placeholders.

The DRHP states no market share, no market rank and no positioning claim, and risk factor 25 describes the interior fit-out industry as highly fragmented and competitive with numerous organized and unorganized players, flagging pricing pressure and margin loss. The Company's own disclosure is that there are no listed companies with similar operations or of comparable size, so an industry comparison is not possible - informative, but it also means no external benchmark exists for the 28.20% stub EBITDA margin. Certification is limited to ISO 9001:2015, with key awards and recognitions recorded as NIL.

Direction is improving on all three axes in the stub: top-5 clients 92.64% (FY2024) and 86.91% (FY2025) to 59.29%; top-10 99.25% to 82.06%; Tamil Nadu 96.45% to 65.34% with Odisha 13.98% and Telangana 11.41% new; top-5 suppliers 44.43% (FY2023) to 33.96%. But the base was near-total dependence, the improvement is one 11-month period old, more than 40 of the 50-plus completed projects are in Tamil Nadu, and no client or supplier is named.

Only 2 tax proceedings against the Company aggregating Rs 61.73 lakhs are disclosed; nil criminal, statutory/regulatory and material civil matters against the Company, Promoters, Directors, Group Company and KMP/SMP, and no SEBI or exchange disciplinary action in five Fiscals. Marked down because contingent liabilities of Rs 143.60 lakhs (BG/LC Rs 81.87 plus GST Rs 61.73, 22.87% of net worth) appear only at February 28, 2026 against dashes in all three prior years, the GST amount is roughly five times the Rs 12.56 lakhs materiality threshold, and insurance excludes loss of profits and terrorism.

Executive depth is two people: Mugundhan Sekar (39, with the Company since incorporation, redesignated Chairman and Managing Director for five years from April 10, 2026, sanctioned salary Rs 12.00 lakhs p.a.) and Ishwarya Packirysamy (34, with the Company since 2017, Whole Time Director from April 10, 2026, sanctioned Rs 3.00 lakhs p.a. with NIL paid in F.Y. 2025-26). The CFO, Company Secretary and both Independent Directors were all appointed on April 10, 2026, two months before the DRHP; the fifth director, Packirysamy Sundaramoorthy, is stated to hold no qualification degree with no experience set out. No headcount, attrition or succession disclosure exists in the routed sections.

Positives: assets equal equity plus liabilities in all four periods (Rs 5,620.49 / 3,138.14 / 2,120.60 / 1,120.88 lakhs), PBT less tax equals PAT, cash-flow subtotals tie to the printed net change, exceptional and extraordinary items are nil throughout, and the basis is unchanged standalone Indian GAAP with a single AS-17 segment. Negatives: an 11-month stub against 12-month years, a change of auditor between FY2024 and FY2025, an unreconciled Rs 49.00 lakhs FY2023 share-issue inflow, an EPS conflict between the restated P&L (Rs 6.36 / 3.00 / 0.99 / 0.62) and the ratio table's pre-bonus series, and Rs 32.05 lakhs of restricted cash sitting inside closing cash.

red_flags: The step-up period's profit is not cash, and the largest object funds the gap. In the 11 months to February 28, 2026 the Company reported revenue of Rs 4,289.31 lakhs and PAT of Rs 753.31 lakhs while CFO was minus Rs 1,158.37 lakhs - the worst of the four periods - on a Rs 1,313.99 lakhs increase in trade receivables (to Rs 1,825.48 lakhs, debtor days 57 to 142) and a Rs 689.48 lakhs increase in inventories (to Rs 2,350.93 lakhs, inventory days 253 to 285). CFO was also negative in FY2023 (minus Rs 128.96 lakhs) and FY2024 (minus Rs 463.03 lakhs); the single positive year, FY2025, was Rs 589.86 lakhs. Closing cash is Rs 54.23 lakhs including Rs 32.05 lakhs restricted, financing inflow for the stub was Rs 1,099.67 lakhs, and Rs 1,500.00 lakhs of the Net Proceeds - the largest single object, ahead of the Rs 760.00 lakhs capex - is earmarked for incremental working capital, with the funding-pattern table placing the entire Rs 1,500.00 lakhs against March 31, 2027.

There is a timing gap between the only plant's lease and the replacement plant, and the document does not address it. The Manufacturing Facility (5,000 sq ft) and the warehouse, both at Krishna Industrial Estate, Vanagaram, Chennai, are on leave and licence from one landlord, Mr K.C. Saravanan, expiring January 03, 2027. The replacement 9,266 sq ft facility at Periyapanichery Village, Kundrathur Taluk, Kancheepuram has no land: risk factor 16 states the land has not been acquired on lease and the lease deed has not been executed or registered, only an MoU dated June 2, 2026 with Mrs Gaffurunnisa Begum @ Gulzar Begum, Mr N. Mahafuz Ul Huq and Mrs N. Haseena Begum exists, and the deed is to be registered only upon utilisation of the Net Proceeds; the stated schedule is registration and approvals in 30-45 days from Net Proceeds, construction 3-4 months, machinery 2-3 months from order placement, commercial operations 6-9 months from receipt of Net Proceeds. Meanwhile all five existing product lines run at 83.19% to 95.22% utilisation, so there is no idle capacity to absorb an interruption.

Every rupee of the Rs 760.00 lakhs capex rests on quotations and an MoU, with no appraisal and no monitoring agency. The DRHP states no definitive agreements have been entered for procurement of the plant and machinery and no purchase orders are stated as placed for any line; the 13 machinery lines are quotations dated May 21-29, 2026 with validity of 60 days, 8 weeks or 180 days, totalling Rs 353.58 lakhs plus Rs 6.45 lakhs transportation/installation against the printed total of Rs 360.00 lakhs (largest single line: Flat Bed CNC Machine, HOMAG India Private Limited, Rs 67.70 lakhs, 8-week validity). Construction is allocated Rs 250.00 lakhs against an engineer-certified Rs 252.88 lakhs (Er. E Packiya, Civil & Structural Engineer, report dated June 11, 2026) and a third-party quotation of Rs 295.26 lakhs (M/s Third Wall Design Studio, June 10, 2026). Risk factor 42 states the deployment has not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency; risk factor 41 states no monitoring agency is appointed because the Issue is below the Rs 5,000.00 lakhs threshold, leaving the audit committee - constituted April 10, 2026 - as the only monitor. The Net Proceeds deployment table (M N H & Co certificate, UDIN 26254857DXXGVP8852) prints a placeholder against every year for every object.

The capital structure was reshaped in the five weeks before filing and the promoters' certified cost is Rs 0.45 a share. Face value was split from Rs 10 to Rs 5 on May 7, 2026 and a 1:10 bonus of 1,15,38,000 shares was allotted on May 08, 2026, taking the count from 11,53,800 to 1,26,91,800 - a bonus issue inside 18 months of the DRHP date. The same May 7, 2026 date carries both the Board resolution and the Section 62(1)(c) special resolution authorising the Issue. Against a promoter average cost of acquisition of Rs 0.45 per share for both Mugundhan Sekar and Ishwarya Packirysamy (55,00,000 shares each, 43.34% each), outside money came in at Rs 780 and Rs 1,000 per pre-split share between July 30 and October 30, 2025. The register holds 19 shareholders in total - 2 promoters at 86.67% and 17 public holders at 13.33% - and alongside the Fresh Issue of up to 60,00,000 shares sits an Offer for Sale of up to 10,00,000 shares whose selling shareholder is not identified in the routed text.

A promoter-controlled entity operates in the same line of business, and the document that would size it is absent. Risk factor 33 names Lifestyle Modular Private Limited as engaged in Interior Designing and states conflicts of interest may arise in allocating business opportunities; the AS 18 note identifies Life Style Modular Private Limited as an enterprise over which the KMPs exercise significant influence, and both Mugundhan Sekar and Ishwarya Packirysamy hold directorships in it. The Company purchased Rs 30.00 lakhs (FY2023), Rs 24.48 lakhs (FY2024) and Rs 48.94 lakhs (FY2025) from it, cross-footing to a trade payable that moved from nil (March 31, 2023) to Rs 24.48 lakhs to Rs 73.42 lakhs (March 31, 2025). A non-compete agreement is asserted but its terms and duration are not stated, no 'Our Group Companies' chapter is present in the routed text, and no revenue, profit or size figure for the entity is available.

Statutory filing and remittance indiscipline is continuous and runs right into the filing window. Risk factor 17 tabulates 24 delayed ROC filings, the worst being an MGT-14 due 29-11-2022 and filed 15-05-2026 - approximately 1,233 days late, and filed the same week as the split and bonus - alongside ADT-1 delays of 339, 254 and 188 days, AOC-4 324 days, MGT-7 294 days, and SH-7 plus PAS-3 178 days each; the most recent are MGT-7A for FY2024-25 (19 days) and an MGT-14 filed 31-01-2026 (48 days). Risk factor 22 lists 17 delayed EPF remittances spanning FY2022-23 to FY2025-26 (worst: December 2025 dues due 15-Jan-26, deposited 23-Feb-26, 39 days) and 16 delayed ESIC remittances (worst 54 days). Risk factor 23 records GSTR-1 delays up to 33 days (December 2025 return filed 13-Feb-26) and GSTR-3B delays up to 41 days (December 2025 return filed 30-Jan-26), continuing into the March 2026 return filed 21 days late.

Contingent liabilities and disclosed litigation both appear for the first time in the stub period and both sit above the Board's own materiality line. At February 28, 2026 contingent liabilities total Rs 143.60 lakhs - bank guarantees and letters of credit Rs 81.87 lakhs and GST-related matters Rs 61.73 lakhs - equal to 22.87% of net worth, against dashes on every line in FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023. The Rs 61.73 lakhs is the entire disclosed tax litigation against the Company (2 proceedings, risk factor 11) and is roughly five times the Board Materiality Policy threshold of Rs 12.56 lakhs fixed on May 08, 2026.

Lender reporting on the very assets that secure the borrowings is qualified and unquantified. The Additional Regulatory Information (Note 33, item 9) states the quarterly returns or statements of current assets filed with banks and financial institutions against security of current assets 'are generally in agreement with the books of accounts except some minor differences which are not material to report'. No amount, period or reconciliation is given and no remediation step is described - while the current assets in question are trade receivables of Rs 1,825.48 lakhs and inventories of Rs 2,350.93 lakhs, and the HDFC facility (Rs 815.61 lakhs drawn) is secured primarily on book debts and stock.

A FY2023 financing inflow is not supported by the share reconciliation in the same document. The Restated Cash Flow Statement for FY2023 prints Rs 49.00 lakhs of 'Proceeds from issue of Share Capital (incl. Securities Premium)', while Annexure 5 shows 5,00,000 shares and Rs 50.00 lakhs of paid-up capital at both the opening and closing of FY2023, with the only FY2023 allotment being the March 27, 2023 conversion of loan into equity (4,90,000 shares at Rs 10). The DRHP text as routed does not explain the difference; recorded as printed and not reconciled here.

The stated repayment object does not map cleanly onto the disclosed debt. Risk factor 30 puts unsecured loans from banks and financial institutions at Rs 650.51 lakhs and risk factor 40 puts secured outstanding debt at Rs 815.61 lakhs, against total borrowings of Rs 1,614.12 lakhs (long-term Rs 285.92, short-term Rs 1,328.20) at February 28, 2026; the object earmarks Rs 240.00 lakhs for full or part repayment of 'certain outstanding unsecured borrowings' without naming a lender, and the routed text does not carry the long-term borrowings annexure, so the facility-level composition cannot be pinned down.

All three financial cross-checks tie in all four periods: total assets equal equity plus liabilities at Rs 5,620.49 / 3,138.14 / 2,120.60 / 1,120.88 lakhs, PBT less tax equals PAT, and CFO + CFI + CFF reconciles to the printed net change in cash in each period - on a single, unchanged basis (standalone Indian GAAP, single AS-17 segment) with no consolidation, amalgamation or merger in the last ten years.

Litigation and encumbrance record is clean as disclosed: the only proceedings anywhere in the DRHP are 2 tax matters against the Company aggregating Rs 61.73 lakhs; nil criminal, statutory/regulatory and material civil proceedings for the Company, Promoters, Directors, the Group Company and KMP/SMP; no SEBI or stock-exchange disciplinary action against the Promoters in the five preceding Fiscals; and nil Promoter shares pledged or otherwise encumbered.

Order book gives partial forward cover: Rs 1,968.19 lakhs of unexecuted contract value out of Rs 4,226.72 lakhs across 12 ongoing projects as on February 28, 2026 (46.57% unexecuted), against more than 50 projects stated as completed in the last three financial years and the stub, of which more than 40 were in Tamil Nadu.

Supplier dependence eased rather than tightened: top-5 suppliers fell from 44.43% of purchases (FY2023) to 33.96% (stub), top-10 from 52.05% to 50.35%, and the DRHP records no instance across all four periods of a supplier terminating arrangements or discontinuing supply.

Outside money went in before the Issue at a real price: Rs 684.39 lakhs of pre-IPO equity was raised in the stub period, including Growmo360 Meridian Fund at Rs 780 per share (July 30, August 14 and September 9, 2025) and further placements at Rs 1,000 per share (October 17, 18 and 30, 2025), both on the pre-split Rs 10 face value; Growmo360 held 6.67% at February 28, 2026 having held nil earlier.
